Malangeni, uMdoni (1 drowned)
death_sites.census_place_name: Umdoni LM (Malangeni not found as a Census place here)

dominant_language_across_sites: isiZulu (Lamontville, the main death site: 83% isiZulu, 11% isiXhosa, 2% English)
warning_language_evidence: No statement on warning language. Witness: SAWS issued a Level 2 warning and authorities advised 'Residents in low-lying areas are urged to seek shelter on higher ground due to the exceptionally high risk of flooding.' IOL headline refers to 'previous community warnings' (article returned 403, content not checked).
notes: KZN CoGTA (via search summary): 7 dead from 24 Feb - Lamontville 5, Chatsworth 1 (house collapsed after mudslide), Malangeni/uMdoni 1 drowned; 1 missing. News24 later said 12 in eThekwini and IOL 15 by mid-March; extra deaths not located. EWN also reports 6 died the previous week when homes collapsed (overlaps the 2025-02-19 event). About 280 Lamontville families relocated to shelters. The Chatsworth main place (62.6% English) may not represent the actual collapse site. Victims' ages/genders are from sources; no language was inferred for individuals. The Census 'Malangeni' (582022) is in Umhlabuyalingana, not uMdoni, so it was not used.

warning_language_evidence: No statement on warning language. SAWS Level 5 alert; officials (AllAfrica): "We strongly urge residents in low-lying areas, and those who are near river banks, to immediately move away and seek shelter on higher ground."
notes: This event's death toll is cumulative ('more than 20 people in the last two months'; 15 in eThekwini 19 Feb-15 Mar per municipality summary), not a separate storm count, so it overlaps the 2025-02 events. No deaths were located for 1-2 March itself (IOL source returned 403). The two sites above are the individually reported mid-March deaths (search summaries of TimesLIVE/IOL/Highway Mail; article text not fetched). The Pinetown victim was swept off the low-lying Gordon Road bridge near Stapleton Road while driving home to Northdene, so she was a motorist, not a resident of the site. Worst-affected areas in the mid-March floods reportedly included Inanda, Ntuzuma, KwaMashu, Pinetown, KwaDabeka and Lamontville.

notes: Daily Maverick: 1 swept away, a man and a woman missing; about 100 displaced, 'most of whom live near a floodline in an informal settlement'. IOL: 3 dead once the 2 missing were recovered on 3 Dec. Municipality: Ward 2 (Shiyabazali, New Hanover) and Ward 7. ECR names the Injasuthi riverbank and states the deceased 'was from Matatiele in the Eastern Cape'. That is the source's statement of origin; no language was inferred. It shows that a place-level Census profile may not describe victims who moved there from elsewhere (e.g. tenants in riverside cottages). The only warning statements were post-event (IFP: 'adhere strictly to weather alerts issued by the South African Weather Service'; MEC: 'follow all weather warnings').

City of Mbombela LM, Mpumalanga (named among hard-hit municipalities)

dominant_language_across_sites: Tshivenda (Tswinga, Tshilapfene), Xitsonga (Giyani villages, Nghomunghomu), Sepedi (Mashishimale, Luckau, Legolaneng, Marulaneng); SiSwati/Xitsonga in Mpumalanga. English is at most 1.94% at every located Limpopo village site.
warning_language_evidence: No statement found on the language of warnings. Daily Maverick (16 Feb 2026, 'Anatomy of a disaster'): the municipality 'communicated warnings from the South African Weather Service through platforms such as social media and local radio stations', but of residents of the worst-affected communities, 'very few had an idea of what this meant. It was assumed it would be a bad storm, just a feature of an average rainy season' (about the Red Level 10 warning; Mbaula village, Giyani visited). The Conversation: warnings 'must be sent out via radio, loudspeakers, SMS, WhatsApp, and local volunteers', and SAWS had to debunk a hoax 'storm called Baron' message. Ramaphosa: 'the government could have done better'.
notes: Toll: 37 (20 Mpumalanga, 17 Limpopo; SABC 19 Jan); Limpopo later 22 (IOL 26 Jan) then 25 with 3 missing (eNCA). Located Limpopo deaths total 12 at 9 sites across 3 home-language zones: the Tshivenda heartland (Thulamela west), Xitsonga (Giyani, Malamulele), and Sepedi (Phalaborwa rural, Sekhukhune, Waterberg). Many victims were children who drowned in rivers or while crossing them. No Mpumalanga death was located by village; searches found only 1 Jan 2026 pre-event deaths (Louisville, Nkomazi; Lilly Mine Road; Ekulindeni missing) that may or may not be in the 20. Mpumalanga rows are affected-area, municipality level only. Tshakhuma (Makhado LM, Census id 968078) was named as affected, not as a death site; not profiled. A separate Conversation piece (June 2026, 'Language matters for disaster warnings') deals with an isiXhosa-speaking community, not this event.

dominant_language_across_sites: Afrikaans (5 of 6 located death sites are Afrikaans-majority towns); English only in Kenilworth; isiXhosa in the most-displaced Khayelitsha settlements
notes: IOL (12 May) lists 6 WC deaths: Knysna, Wynberg (Cape Town), George, Worcester, Genadendal, Klaarstroom - most from falling trees rather than flooding. GroundUp/DM give the Cape Town tree death as Kenilworth. The toll later rose to 10 (IOL 14 May) with no locations for the extra 4. SAWS issued an Orange Level 8 disruptive-rainfall warning (4 May). Unlike the other events, most located deaths are in Afrikaans-majority places and are not flood-drowning in informal settlements. Flooding hit 26 informal settlements in Cape Town (Khayelitsha, Philippi etc.), with ~2,000 homes flooded or destroyed. No Eastern Cape or Free State deaths were located.

Tshelimnyama, Ward 15, Mariannhill (most severely affected: mudslides collapsed ~3 houses, 14 residents affected; no deaths)

warning_language_evidence: Not about language directly, but about comprehension. IOL (19 Sep 2026), groundWork's Thalia Erwin: "People do not understand the warnings" ... "What is a level 4 and what does that mean?"; she warned that repeated alerts could cause 'warning fatigue'. IOL does not say which language(s) warnings were issued in. SAWS had issued Orange Level 6 and Yellow Level 4 warnings.
notes: All 4 deaths were road crashes partly attributed to rain; no flood-drowning deaths were confirmed. Road-crash sites describe where vehicle occupants died, not where they lived. Flooded settlements with no deaths: Quarry Road informal settlement (Durban), Melody Hills Transitional Emergency Accommodation (Umlazi), Tshelimnyama (mudslides). The Gingindlovu main place is the small town, not the surrounding isiZulu rural area (uMlalazi LM: isiZulu 92.11, English 3.52).
